conviction_note: The two measurements sit near zero for different reasons: the findings net to +0.2 because a September-30 book value likely a touch worse than the two peer pre-announcements (DX was ~80% hedged vs ~100% at ORC and IVR) is offset by an October-to-date recovery the call will disclose and a short build; p_up 48 and abs_move 3.0 because the stock already fell 18.6% since July to ~1.0x the peer-implied book value, and DX's own prints (max 1.8% in seven) show the market handicaps BV well.
bar: Book value per common share $12.90 at 2026-06-30 (company Q2 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000826675/000082667526000074/a2q26earningsrelease.htm). The market's implied Q3 bar is derived, not published: spot $10.89 is 0.844x June BV, and KBW ($15 -> $12.50, 2026-10-07) and BTIG ($14.50 -> $12.00, 2026-10-06) cut targets ~17%, so the street sits near a -15% to -17% BV decline (~$10.75-11.00). EPS bar is single-sourced (Benzinga non-GAAP $0.53, revenue $104.6M), so the EPS finding is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 17.54M shares at the 2026-09-30 FINRA settlement, 7.1% of shares outstanding, 2.15 days to cover (Equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/dx/shortinterest, fetched 2026-10-16), up from ~10.4M / 4.2% of float / 1.6 DTC at the 2026-08-21 snapshot on the same page: shorts built ~70% into the print but 7% is not crowded. Option chain unusable (ATM spread 120% of mid, 1,866 total OI, put/call OI 1.09), so no skew statement exists. Stock sits 3% off its 52-week low, -10.6% over 20 days.

findings.finding: Two Agency-only peers pre-announced September-30 book value down ~16% in Q3: Orchid Island $6.02 vs $7.22 at June 30 (-16.6%, total return on equity -12.5%, 8-K 2026-10-14) and Invesco Mortgage Capital $6.74 vs $8.03 (-16.1%; monthly path $7.75 at Jul 31, $7.74 at Aug 31, so -12.9% in September alone). Both were ~100% notional-hedged (ORC hedges $10.25B vs $10.36B repo; IVR $6.8B vs $6.8B repo). DX at June 30 carried $14.09B swaps + $4.26B Treasury futures (+$0.75B swaptions) against $23.2B of liabilities, ~79-82% hedged, at 8.1x leverage; in Q1 2026, the last spread-widening quarter, DX's BV fell 6.3% vs ORC -6.1% and AGNC -5.6%. The 10-year rose from 4.42% (Jun 30) to 5.29% (Sep 30) and Agency MBS posted ~-96bp of excess return in September. Read-through: DX Sept-30 BV about $10.3-11.0 (-15% to -20%) vs $12.90; the market-implied bar is ~$10.75-11.00, so the lower hedge ratio puts the central estimate at or slightly below the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline: seven prints, median |move| 0.81%, max 1.8%. The Q1 2026 print (BV -6.3%, the largest decline in the set) moved +0.81%; the Q2 2026 print (BV +2.4%) moved -1.58%. The stock prices BV intra-quarter and the print itself has moved little.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the stock is -18.6% since the July print and -15.5% from $12.89 on Sep 8, to 1.0x the peer-implied BV. What is not visibly priced is the hedge-ratio gap: if the market expected DX to print worse than the ~100%-hedged peers, the stock would sit below ~$10.5 (a discount to the implied book), and the sell-side would not be holding Buy/Outperform with targets 10-15% above spot.

September MBS excess return -96bp (Fidelity, https://institutional.fidelity.com/app/proxy/content?literatureURL=%2F931730.PDF) and MBS-Treasury spread +13bp to 125bp (AGNC data via https://ph.investing.com/news/economy-news/us-treasury-yields-surge-putting-a-chain-reaction-in-focus-2625092). 10-year 4.42% on 2026-06-30 (https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/202606307321/10-year-treasury-yield-rises-to-4420-data-talk) and 5.29% on 2026-09-30 (https://www.mortgagenewsdaily.com/treasury/10yr). This is a peer-and-sensitivity proxy for DX's own number; DX's 10-Q Item 3 sensitivity table could not be read (SEC render truncated, mirror 403).

findings.finding: DX discloses an intra-quarter book value on its call (Q2 call, July 20: 'The book value as of Friday was $12.67', i.e. -1.8% from June 30 by July 17). Since the Sept 30 quarter-end the 10-year has fallen from 5.29% to ~5.09% (Oct 15 close, -11bp on the day; H.15 shows 5.22/5.24/5.21/5.19 for Oct 8-14) and the Agency MBS basis tightened from a one-year high set early in the week of Oct 12 (Nuveen weekly). An Oct 16 'book value as of Friday' several percent above the Sept 30 figure will be stated on the 10:00 ET call, inside the window, alongside a Sept-30 print the peers have already framed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history: the July 17 figure given on the Q2 call was below the June 30 BV and the stock moved -1.58% that day. Peers' Sept-30 8-Ks (ORC, IVR) gave no October-to-date figure, so DX's would be the first October mark from an Agency mREIT.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock has risen ~3% from its Oct 7 close of $10.57 (10-year 5.22%) to $10.89 as the 10-year fell to 5.09%. If the market had fully priced an October BV recovery of 3-5% on top of a -16% Sept-30 print, the stock would be nearer $11.2-11.4 (1.0x the recovered book) rather than $10.89.

This is a rates-to-book-value proxy; the company has not published an October figure.

findings.finding: Short interest rose from ~10.4M shares (4.2% of float, 1.6 days to cover) at the Aug 21 snapshot to 17.54M (7.1% of shares outstanding, 2.15 days to cover) at the Sept 30 FINRA settlement, a ~70% build into the print, with no usable option chain to hedge in (ATM spread 120% of mid, 1,866 contracts OI).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No instance in the seven-print baseline where positioning visibly drove the reaction; all seven moves were under 2%.
findings.why_not_priced: The build is recent (settlements of Sep 15 and Sep 30, published early October) and small in absolute terms; if a squeeze were being priced the stock would not sit 3% off its 52-week low. At 7% of shares and 2 days to cover it is a mild mechanism, not a crowded short.
findings.independence: Baseline options block: put/call OI 1.09, total OI 1,866 (sealed 2026-10-16). None from a second short-interest source; Benzinga's undated 5.75M figure conflicts and was rejected.

findings.finding: DX priced $120M of 9.375% Series D cumulative preferred on Sep 22 (4.8M shares at $25, net ~$115.9M, 720k-share greenshoe, closed Sep 29; common closed $12.07 on Sep 21 per the $6.035 share-cap in the prospectus) with stated use of proceeds 'to finance the acquisition of Agency and other investment securities'. The money buys Agency MBS at the widest spreads in a year (basis 125bp at Sept 30) rather than funding a de-leveraging; it also costs ~$11.3M/yr of preferred dividends (~$0.045/common share) and ~$4M of issuance cost (~$0.02/share of BV), and tells the market management chose to hold or add risk through the September selloff.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prior capital raises were common ATM issuance ($442M in Q1, $391M in Q2) described by management as accretive; neither print moved more than 1.6%. No prior preferred issuance in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: The raise itself is public and priced (stock fell $12.07 -> $11.18 from Sep 21 to Sep 25, coinciding with the 10-year hitting 5.2%). What the print adds is whether the capital was deployed at wide spreads (raising forward NII per share) or held as liquidity; the 42c of Q2 NII against a 51c dividend makes that the live question on the call.
findings.independence: Pricing press release and underwriting agreement: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000826675/000082667526000104/exhibit991preferredofferin.htm (2026-09-22); closing and articles of amendment: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/826675/000082667526000112/dx-20260929.htm (2026-09-29); Q2 call NII 42c vs dividend 51c: https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/DX/Q22026. Shares the Q2 transcript with finding 2.

findings.finding: Chief Investment Officer Terrence Connelly Jr. bought 2,500 DX shares in the open market at $11.18 on 2026-09-25 (Form 4 code P, holdings 58,695 after), three days after the preferred priced and during the worst week of the MBS selloff; Chairman Byron Boston's Sep 8 Form 4 was a tax-withholding (code F) of 15,667 shares at $12.89, not a sale.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No instance in the baseline where an insider transaction preceded a print; the purchase is ~$28k, small against the CIO's existing stake.
findings.why_not_priced: A $28k purchase is too small to move a $2.7bn name and the stock fell a further 5% after it; it is filed as a weak signal that the insider with the best view of the hedge book bought at $11.18, above today's $10.89, i.e. he did not see book value below that level on Sep 25.
findings.independence: Boston Form 4: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/826675/000082667526000089/wk-form4_1789075326.xml (2026-09-08). None pointing the same way from an unrelated source.

findings.finding: Consensus non-GAAP EPS for Q3 is $0.53 on Benzinga against a Q2 print of $0.36 (vs $0.50 estimate) and Q1 $0.31, both misses; Q2 net interest income was 42c per share against a 51c quarterly dividend ($0.17 monthly, held for October on Oct 12, record Oct 22). A 16% smaller equity base, ~10M more shares issued in July (237.4M at Jun 30 to 247.4M at Jul 24) and the new 9.375% preferred make a fourth consecutive miss on that line likely, with dividend coverage the question on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 missed on this line ($0.36 vs $0.50) and the stock moved -1.58%; Q1 2026 missed ($0.31) and moved +0.81%. The market has not traded DX on this EPS line. The dividend for October is already declared, so no cut can land inside the window; the November declaration (~Nov 10) is outside it.
findings.why_not_priced: Capped small: the EPS bar has one source and DX does not publish an EAD measure, so the 'miss' is partly a definitional artefact; the three prior misses moved the stock less than 2%.
findings.independence: Q2 call NII 42c and dividend 51c: https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/DX/Q22026 (shares the Q2 transcript with findings 2 and 4). Share count from the 10-Q cover: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/826675/000082667526000078/dx-20260630.htm (2026-07-27). October dividend: https://finviz.com/news/401422/dynex-capital-inc-declares-october-monthly-common-stock-dividend-of-017 (2026-10-12).

findings.finding: Common share count rose from 237,414,259 at June 30 to 247,429,551 at July 24 (~10M ATM shares in 3-4 weeks at ~$12.6-13.0, around the $12.67-12.90 book), and on July 28 the ATM program was upsized by 80M shares to 301.3M with 99.3M remaining, so further August/September issuance at or near book is likely before the stock broke below book in mid-September; BV-neutral but it raises the share count the Q3 per-share figures are divided by.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 ($442M) and Q2 ($391M) ATM raises were disclosed at the print and management called them accretive; neither print moved more than 1.6%.
findings.why_not_priced: Issuance at ~1.0x book neither creates nor destroys BV per share; filed at zero so the judges can see the Q3 share count will be higher than June's and that per-share EPS comparisons to Q2 are not like-for-like.
findings.independence: 10-Q cover share count: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/826675/000082667526000078/dx-20260630.htm (2026-07-27); ATM capacity restated in the Series D prospectus supplement (2026-09-22). No source states Q3 issuance after July 24.

outside_window.finding: AGNC reports Q3 2026 after the close on 2026-10-19 with its call at 08:30 ET on 2026-10-20: the sector's bellwether tangible book value (June 30 $8.58, hedge ratio 73% of funding liabilities, closer to DX's ~80% than to ORC/IVR's ~100%) and its October-to-date commentary land after a bmo window that closes at the Oct 19 close.
Annaly reports after the close on 2026-10-20 (company-attributed date per Therighttrader, conflicting aggregator dates Oct 27/28); ARMOUR on 2026-10-28; both after the window.

The November monthly dividend declaration (~2026-11-10) is where a cut from $0.17 would be visible; the October dividend was already declared at $0.17 on Oct 12 (record Oct 22, paid Nov 2). ORC already pays $0.10 and IVR $0.12 monthly after Q3.

baseline_tension: No skew exists (chain unusable); the run-up is -10.6% over 20 days to 3% off the 52-week low, and the findings mostly agree with it: the peer-implied -16% book value is what the drawdown already priced, the October rates recovery and the short build cut mildly against it, and the net is near zero.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (positioning): short-interest finding cut from +0.5 to +0.4 because 7.1% of shares and 2.15 days to cover is a build, not a crowded short
Rule 6 (verify the bar): EPS finding kept at -0.3 and explicitly capped because the $0.53 consensus has one source and DX publishes no EAD measure
Rule 4 (financing): Series D finding kept at +0.3; the use of proceeds (Agency MBS at wide spreads) was checked before signing
Rule 1 and the reaction history: p_up left at 48 and abs_move at 3.0; DX's seven prints under 2% already damped the reaction read
Rule 3: finding 1 (Sept-30 BV down) and finding 2 (October recovery) are different dates and both can be true; left as separate findings
